summary: This PR replaces the Greeting screen with a Quiz screen: a scrolling list of 10 cards, each with a three-state checkbox. It also commits IDE settings. The checkbox click handler won't compile, and once that's fixed, each answer is lost when its card scrolls off screen or the device rotates.

accepted.title: The checkbox click handler does not compile
accepted.whatGoesWrong: A three-state checkbox's click callback receives no value. The handler `{ state = it }` uses `it`, which does not exist there. The app fails to build.
accepted.whyItMatters: Nothing can run or be tested until this compiles.
accepted.howToFix: Pass a handler with no arguments that moves to the next state. For example: `onClick = { state = if (state == ToggleableState.On) ToggleableState.Off else ToggleableState.On }`, or rotate through all three states.

accepted.title: Quiz answers are lost when a card scrolls off screen or the device rotates
accepted.whatGoesWrong: Each card keeps its checkbox state with `remember` inside the scrolling list. The list throws away cards that scroll out of view. When the user ticks a few answers, scrolls down and comes back, those cards are reset to the 'indeterminate' state. Rotating the screen resets all of them.
accepted.whyItMatters: Users silently lose their quiz answers.
accepted.howToFix: Keep the answers outside the list items, for example in a list of 10 states held in a ViewModel or a `rememberSaveable` list in `Quiz`, and read each card's state by its index. At minimum, use `rememberSaveable` instead of `remember`.
